title: Electroencephalogram biomarkers as predictors of mortality and functional recovery in patients with severe traumatic brain injury: Protocol study
author: Filho, do Nascimento Moura, et al.

steps.title: Define eligibility and obtain consent
steps.instruction: Screen all trauma admissions for adults ≥ 18 years, Glasgow Coma Scale ≤ 8, open traumatic brain injury, and ICU admission; exclude patients under 18, with prior neurological or psychiatric disease, or without signed informed consent; record eligibility in daily logs and obtain consent before any data collection.

substeps.instruction: Inclusion: age ≥ 18, GCS ≤ 8, open TBI, ICU admission.
Exclusion: age < 18, previous neurological disease, previous psychiatric disease, no signed consent.

steps.title: Calculate required sample size
steps.instruction: Use GPower to perform a two‑tailed hypothesis test for a Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.3, significance level α = 0.05, and power = 0.80, which yields a target sample size of 84 participants.

steps.title: Schedule EEG recording in subacute phase
steps.instruction: Plan EEG acquisition to begin on day 7 or later after the traumatic event (subacute phase) and perform the recording immediately after the patient is transferred from the ICU to the hospital ward.

steps.title: Prepare patient scalp for EEG
steps.instruction: Instruct the patient to wash hair with neutral shampoo and ensure it is completely dry; apply conductive gel to each electrode site before placement.

steps.title: Configure EEG system
steps.instruction: Set up the Starstim® 20‑channel system (Startism 20) with a time constant of 0.3 seconds and a high‑frequency cutoff of 30 Hz; conduct the recording in a quiet environment with low lighting.

steps.title: Place electrodes and verify impedance
steps.instruction: Position electrodes according to the international 10‑20 system, using the earlobes as reference; adjust each electrode until its impedance is below 3 kΩ.

steps.title: Record resting‑state EEG
steps.instruction: Record EEG while the patient is resting, relaxed, awake, and eyes closed, ensuring the environment remains quiet and low‑lit.

steps.title: Administer functional outcome scales
steps.instruction: At ICU discharge, hospital discharge, and at 3, 6, and 12 months post‑TBI, assess the patient using the Glasgow Coma Scale, Dementia Rating Scale, Functional Independence Measure, Functional Ambulation Categories, and Rancho Los Amigos Scale as described.

steps.title: Preprocess EEG data
steps.instruction: Import EEG recordings into MATLAB with the EEGLAB plugin, apply noise filtering, remove artifacts, and extract frequency and amplitude features of the brain‑wave bands.

steps.title: Conduct statistical analyses
steps.instruction: Use SPSS v28 for descriptive statistics, normality testing (Shapiro‑Wilk), and group comparisons (t‑test, Mann‑Whitney, or ANOVA as appropriate); perform binomial logistic regression in Stata v17; generate ROC curves and calculate AUC in SPSS, validating models with cross‑validation and the Hosmer‑Lemeshow test.
